listHtml.registerNote: Owned by ONE person (a username) or ONE application (its identifier). A key typed here is public material — a PEM certificate, a public JWK, or the credential id of a security key the owner enrolled — and is recorded as proven by nobody and self-asserted. A person at devices.maxPerPerson is refused rather than losing a device to make room.
listHtml.label: Label
listHtml.appsHint: client ids or identifiers, comma separated
listHtml.keyHint: PEM, JWK JSON or credential id
listHtml.readOnly: Registering, editing or removing a device needs Admin Write.
listHtml.leadIntro: Every device this realm knows, each an entry under ou=devices owned by one person or one application.
listHtml.leadSame: is the same register attribute by attribute;
listHtml.noMatch: No device matches. The filter above may be hiding some.
deviceHtml.ssoLive: a secret, bound to a live sign-on session
deviceHtml.ssoEnded: a secret whose sign-on session has ended
deviceHtml.keysNote: Each is a way the device is recognised. The thumbprint is SHA-256 over the certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, or RFC 7638 over the JWK — which is DPoP's jkt.
deviceHtml.complianceNote: An administrator's vouch, recorded with source admin. A change a receiver can be told — CAEP knows compliant and not-compliant, and unknown is sent as not-compliant — goes out as CAEP device-compliance-change.
deviceHtml.compromisedNote: This device is marked compromised. Restoring it puts back the risk level the compromise raised; nothing revoked comes back — a certificate is re-issued and a Native SSO secret re-minted at the next sign-in.
deviceHtml.markNote: Marking it compromised ends every sign-on session one of its keys authenticated, revokes its Native SSO secret and every certificate this service's EST or SCEP Issuing CA issued it (keyCompromise), raises its risk level to HIGH, and — for a person's device — sends RISC credential-compromise (and sessions-revoked, where risc.autoEmitTypes names it). It stays in the register, recognised and saying so.
deviceHtml.addKeyNote: Public material only; recorded as proven by nobody and self-asserted.
deviceHtml.label: Label
deviceHtml.editNote: A new owner takes the device without its Native SSO secret, which was bound to the old owner's session; its keys go with it. The applications field replaces the list.
deviceHtml.removeNote: Removing it revokes the certificates this service issued it (cessationOfOperation, or keyCompromise when it is compromised) and ends the sign-on sessions it authenticated.
androidStatusHtml.heading: Android attestation status list
androidStatusHtml.noteBefore: Every certificate of an Android Key Attestation chain — at a device's registration and at a WebAuthn android-key statement — is looked up in Google's list of revoked and suspended attestation certificates. A chain it names is not attested. The list is the risk dataset android.attestation-status on
androidStatusHtml.noteAfter: , downloaded by {job} from {from, select, url {{url}} other {nowhere (devices.androidStatusUrl is empty; upload it on Risk)}}.
androidStatusHtml.noList: none — Android chains are recorded with their revocation UNCHECKED
androidStatusHtml.stillAttested: is still attested, with the reason recorded (devices.androidRevocationRequired is off)
registrationHtml.leadBefore: A device is an entry under ou=devices, owned by ONE person or ONE application, holding the keys it is recognised by.
registrationHtml.leadAfter: is the register; this page is how a device gets into it and how it is known again.
registrationHtml.attestationNote: A device is attested when a verifier checked an attestation statement for one of its keys and it chained to a trust anchor below, and self-asserted otherwise. The formats it records: {formats}. A statement that does not verify is refused in both modes; one that verifies and chains to nothing here is self-asserted.
registrationHtml.selfAssertedAccepted: This realm (development) registers a self-asserted key a device or its owner presents.
registrationHtml.selfAssertedRefused: This realm (product) REFUSES a self-asserted key a device or its owner presents (STS-DEVICE-0024).
registrationHtml.freshRequired: A TPM key attestation must also be FRESH: its extraData a nonce from {nonce}, sent with that response's cookie, or it is refused (STS-DEVICE-0050).
registrationHtml.freshUnproven: A TPM key attestation that is not fresh (no nonce from {nonce}) is recorded with freshness unproven.
registrationHtml.challengesNote: The challenges /portal/devices issues are held in {store}, per realm and persisted, one per session and purpose, answered once across the cluster and for {ttl} seconds; {live} are live, of at most {max}.
registrationHtml.recordedHeading: Where a recognised device is recorded
registrationHtml.recordedNote: At a sign-in: {signIn}. At the token endpoint: {token}. A compromised device is still recognised, and says so.
registrationHtml.complianceNote: A device is compliant, not-compliant or unknown (where it starts); every change records its previous value and who set it — {sources}.
registrationHtml.adminBefore: Set compliance on a device's page under
registrationHtml.mdmHow: {path} with an access token carrying {scope} — a PROTECTED scope, issued only to a client that declares it, and the only scope that operation takes: the feed needs no admin scope and gets none. Up to {max} reports, each naming its device by {by}. Source mdm, the client as actor.
registrationHtml.caepBefore: From a federation partner whose Shared Signals this realm receives — a device manager is an ssf relationship on
registrationHtml.caepMiddle: — as the signal-response policy permits (#373, #374), its device named by id or key thumbprint. Source caep; arrivals on
registrationHtml.signalsHeading: What goes out over Shared Signals
registrationHtml.signalsNote: CAEP: {caep}. RISC, for a person's device compromised or removed: {risc}. The subject is {subject}. A compliance change goes out only when what a receiver can be told moved: CAEP knows compliant and not-compliant, and unknown is sent as not-compliant.
registrationHtml.decidesNote: Risk scoring: the signals {signals} — the last two lower the score; unregistered-device fires {expect, select, yes {for anybody here (devices.expectRegistered)} other {only for a person who registered a device}}. The issuance policy ({policy}): a compromised device is {refuse, select, yes {refused} other {only a risk signal}}; a compliant registered device is {require, select, yes {required} attested {required, and attested} other {not required (off by default)}}. The acr {acr}, and the claim {claim}.
monitorHtml.leadBefore: What this realm's register holds, counted now, and what happened to it: every registration, removal, and eviction at a person's devices.maxPerPerson, kept up to devices.eventsKept, and every compliance change by who made it — admin, mdm, test-control, caep
monitorHtml.leadAfter: . A device removed by an ldapdelete on the socket is not an event here — the register never sees it.
monitorHtml.countersNote: Counted in this process since it started ({scope}): a page served by one node of a cluster shows that node's.
monitorHtml.enrolments: Enrolments by a device or its owner, by method
